expected_symptom: With -P, dxc must print the same "; Opening file [<header>], stack top [<n>]" lines that -H prints on a normal compile of the same source; today it prints nothing at all.
godbolt_skip: Not demonstrable on CE, measured not assumed (manual-case-ce-infeasible.txt, dxc_trunk). The symptom is a MISSING include trace, so a pane must contain a real #include and a header beside it; a CE pane is single-source. Measured on CE: (1) with no #include, -H prints no trace at all, so the working case cannot be shown either; (2) a pane that #includes its own header gets "fatal error: file not found"; (3) -P additionally renders as <No output file>. An empty CE output pane would be indistinguishable from nothing having run, which is worse than no link.
summary: Still absent on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and in all 21 stable releases v1.4.1907-v1.9.2607: -H/-Vi are accepted under -P (an unknown dash-flag in the same position exits 1) but produce no output and leave the preprocessed bytes identical (SHA-256). Not a design decision -- the trace IS generated under -P and IS stored as DXC_OUT_REMARKS (verified through IDxcCompiler3, with controls); DxcContext::Compile() prints REMARKS (dxc.cpp:918) and DxcContext::Preprocess() (dxc.cpp:1005) never reads it, and the combination is absent from the "options ignored with Preprocess" warning list. Since v1.7.2207 -M lists dependencies and composes with -H, but only in compile mode. Linear grammar-aware release sweep, because -P changed grammar at 8bf2b087c.
title: Support -H and -P at the same time
